title: When the Wreck Sings
premise: Casper Joubert, a nonbinary riverboat captain who has spent twenty years ferrying cargo and secrets along the Kestrel River, discovers a tide-revealed sea cave holding the wreck of the Meridian—a lost expedition vessel whose manifest includes proof that Casper's late mentor, Old Tam, was not who he claimed to be. When a salvage consortium and a journalist converge on the river, Casper must lead the expedition to the wreck while deciding whether to bury or reveal the truth about Tam's identity—and their own. Betrayed by a crew member selling coordinates, Casper races a storm and the consortium to the cave, and in the end chooses truth: they surface the wreck, claim Tam's legacy openly under their own name, and finally stop measuring life in miles.
about_author: Casper Brightwater spent a decade working seasonal jobs on inland waterways before turning to writing, and their fiction is steeped in the rhythms of river towns and the people who never quite settle there. They live on a restored sternwheeler with a dog named Barge and write only when the fog lifts.

chapters.title: Low Water, Old Ghosts
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A routine cargo run down the Kestrel establishes Casper's mastery of the river and their carefully maintained anonymity—no fixed address, no past discussed. An unusually low tide exposes a sea cave mouth no chart records. Emotional beat: restless unease beneath competent calm.

chapters.title: The Cave That Charges Admission
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Against instinct, Casper explores the cave at slack tide and finds timbers, a brass nameplate—Meridian—and a sealed strongbox bearing Tam's initials. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread, because Tam swore he'd never sailed salt water.

chapters.title: What Tam Left in the Box
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, with flashback. In the boat's cabin, Casper opens the strongbox: letters, a photograph of a woman, and documents suggesting Tam was a disgraced expedition navigator who faked his death. Emotional beat: grief complicated by betrayal; loyalty begins to war with truth.

chapters.title: The Consortium Arrives
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Casper and Vesper Kline, the consortium's sharp salvage scout. Kline arrives in town asking about 'unusual tides,' waving permits and money. Casper plays dumb. Emotional beat: the first pressure on Casper's invisibility; the river town's gossip becomes a threat.

chapters.title: Crew of Necessity
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper assembles a small crew—engineer Dovie, deckhand Rill, and old friend Marisol—claiming a 'survey job.' Rill asks too many questions. Emotional beat: the warmth of chosen family shadowed by the weight of the lie Casper is already telling them.

chapters.title: The Journalist on the Dock
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Freelance journalist Theo Anand corners Marisol about the Meridian legend; Marisol deflects but is shaken—she recognizes the name from Tam's stories. Emotional beat: loyalty tested by curiosity, and the first hint that Tam's past has more witnesses than Casper knew.

chapters.title: Charting the Impossible
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Planning the expedition, Casper realizes the cave is only accessible at a specific spring tide—nine days away, and the consortium's survey barge will beat them there unless Casper offers to 'guide' them on a false route. Emotional beat: cold resolve; Casper decides to control the story rather than hide from it.

chapters.title: Rill's Side Deal
chapters.summary: Rill's POV. Pressured by debts, Rill photographs Casper's charts and texts a buyer—Kline. Immediately guilt-ridden, Rill deletes nothing and confesses nothing. Emotional beat: fear and rationalization; the betrayal that will drive the climax is set in motion.

chapters.title: Upstream Lies
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper leads the consortium's barge up a dead slough, buying two days, while Dovie quietly rigs the boat for a real run. Kline watches Casper too closely. Emotional beat: the thrill and cost of deception; Casper recognizes Tam's habits in themselves.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Photograph
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper tracks down the photograph's subject, Ada Voss—now elderly—in a river town upstream. Ada reveals Tam was her brother, lost on the Meridian's final voyage, and that he survived and chose erasure. Emotional beat: compassion reframing betrayal; Tam's lie was shelter, not malice.

chapters.title: Nine Days Becomes Four
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo publishes a teaser about the Meridian's location 'narrowing,' and the consortium accelerates, chartering divers. Casper learns the spring tide window is shrinking due to an early storm system. Emotional beat: ticking clock tightens; the river itself becomes an adversary.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol confronts Casper with Ada's name, forcing a partial confession. Casper shares the letters but not the plan. Marisol chooses loyalty—but tells Theo a half-truth to buy time. Emotional beat: intimacy forged through shared secrecy, and its fragility.

chapters.title: The Mutiny of Small Doubts
chapters.summary: Dovie's POV. Dovie notices Rill's nervousness and the boat's altered trim, suspects a second secret, and quietly prepares life rafts. The crew's trust frays in small, human ways. Emotional beat: dread without evidence; the reader sees the betrayal closing in.

chapters.title: Coordinates for Sale
chapters.summary: Kline's POV. Kline receives Rill's coordinates, cross-references the tide tables, and realizes Casper has been playing them. Kline doesn't confront—Kline sets a trap, offering Rill full payment for a meeting aboard the barge. Emotional beat: the antagonist's cold competence; the noose draws.

chapters.title: The Run to the Cave
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. At the spring tide's edge, Casper makes the real run through fog and shifting sandbars, Dovie at the engine, Marisol on the lead line. They reach the cave mouth as the consortium's lights appear downstream. Emotional beat: exhilaration and terror fused—the river at its most alive.

chapters.title: Inside the Meridian
chapters.summary: Casper and Marisol's POV, alternating. Diving the wreck at slack water, they find the expedition's true cargo: not treasure, but Tam's logbook proving the original expedition's sponsor falsified the disaster to cover embezzlement—making Tam's disappearance both flight and testimony. Emotional beat: revelation that transforms Tam from betrayer to witness.

chapters.title: Rill's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Rill's POV. Kline springs the trap, revealing Rill's texts and demanding the cave's interior layout in exchange for erasing the debt. Rill refuses—and is locked aboard the barge as it steams for the cave. Emotional beat: shame transmuting into the resolve to undo the damage.

chapters.title: Storm Tide
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. The early storm arrives with the tide; the consortium barge grounds on the bar Casper falsified, taking on water. Casper faces the choice the whole book has built toward: slip away with the truth, or turn back to rescue the people hunting them. Emotional beat: the climax's moral fulcrum.

chapters.title: The Rescue
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper threads the storm-lifted river to pull Kline's crew and Rill off the wrecked barge, nearly losing the boat. Rill confesses everything to Casper mid-rescue. Emotional beat: grace under pressure; loyalty proven not by words but by turning the wheel around.

chapters.title: What the Wreck Sings
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. With the storm passing and the consortium's credibility wrecked by the grounding and the embezzlement evidence, Casper surfaces the Meridian's logbook publicly—naming Tam, naming the sponsor, and naming themselves. Emotional beat: catharsis; invisibility voluntarily ended.

chapters.title: Miles and Years
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Aftermath: the salvage claim resolved, Ada Voss visits the boat, Rill stays aboard working off trust mile by mile, and Theo writes the story Casper helped shape. Casper charts a new route with a home port at last. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace.

chapters.title: The Next Tide
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, coda. A letter arrives from a historian asking Casper to consult on another lost vessel; Kline, humbled, offers partnership instead of acquisition. Casper looks at the cave mouth at low tide—now a known place, a named place—and says yes. Emotional beat: identity claimed; the river, and the future, open.
